6: # On-Call Handoff Patterns
7: 
8: Effective patterns for on-call shift transitions, ensuring continuity, context transfer, and reliable incident response across shifts.
9: 
10: ## When to Use This Skill
11: 
12: - Transitioning on-call responsibilities
13: - Writing shift handoff summaries
14: - Documenting ongoing investigations
15: - Establishing on-call rotation procedures
16: - Improving handoff quality
17: - Onboarding new on-call engineers
18: 
19: ## Core Concepts
20: 
21: ### 1. Handoff Components
22: 
23: | Component                  | Purpose                 |
24: | -------------------------- | ----------------------- |
25: | **Active Incidents**       | What's currently broken |
26: | **Ongoing Investigations** | Issues being debugged   |
27: | **Recent Changes**         | Deployments, configs    |
28: | **Known Issues**           | Workarounds in place    |
29: | **Upcoming Events**        | Maintenance, releases   |
30: 
31: ### 2. Handoff Timing
32: 
33: ```
34: Recommended: 30 min overlap between shifts
35: 
36: Outgoing:
37: ├── 15 min: Write handoff document
38: └── 15 min: Sync call with incoming
39: 
40: Incoming:
41: ├── 15 min: Review handoff document
42: ├── 15 min: Sync call with outgoing
43: └── 5 min: Verify alerting setup
44: ```
45: 
46: ## Templates and detailed worked examples
47: 
48: Full template library and detailed worked examples live in `references/details.md`. Read that file when you need the concrete templates.
49: 
50: ## Troubleshooting
51: 
52: **Incoming engineer misses a critical issue because the handoff document was incomplete.**
53: Use the outgoing checklist as a gate: do not mark handoff complete until every section has at least one entry (or an explicit "none"). Make incomplete handoffs a blameless postmortem action item.
54: 
55: **A 30-minute sync call is not possible due to timezone gaps.**
56: Fall back to the async quick handoff template (Template 2). Supplement with a short Loom or voice memo walking through the watch list. Ensure the incoming engineer has a direct contact method if they have follow-up questions.
57: 
58: **The incoming engineer inherits a mid-incident and is immediately overwhelmed.**
59: Use the incident handoff template (Template 3) specifically. The outgoing engineer should remain available on Slack for 15 minutes after handoff, even if off-call, to answer clarifying questions.
60: 
61: **On-call handoff documents are inconsistently formatted across teams.**
62: Adopt the shift handoff template organization-wide and store completed handoffs in a shared location (wiki, Notion, Confluence). Link each handoff from the on-call schedule entry in PagerDuty.
63: 
64: **Incoming engineer cannot verify their alerting is working before the outgoing engineer logs off.**
65: Add a standard step: outgoing engineer fires a test alert and confirms incoming engineer receives it in PagerDuty and Slack before ending the overlap window.
66: 
67: ## Related Skills
68: 
69: - [incident-classification](../../skills/incident-classification/SKILL.md) — Classify and prioritize incidents that need to be included in the handoff document
70: - [postmortem-facilitation](../../skills/postmortem-facilitation/SKILL.md) — Turn resolved incidents from the shift into structured postmortems", "references/details.md": "1: # on-call-handoff-patterns — templates and worked examples

26: ### 1. Intermittent API Timeouts (ENG-1234)
27: 
28: **Status**: Investigating
29: **Started**: 2024-01-20
30: **Impact**: ~0.1% of requests timing out
31: 
32: **Context**:
33: 
34: - Timeouts correlate with database backup window (02:00-03:00 UTC)

50: ### 2. Memory Growth in Auth Service (ENG-1235)
51: 
52: **Status**: Monitoring
53: **Started**: 2024-01-18
54: **Impact**: None yet (proactive)

56: **Context**:
57: 
58: - Memory usage growing ~5% per day

75: 
76: ### Payment Service Outage (2024-01-19)
77: 
78: - **Duration**: 23 minutes
79: - **Root Cause**: Database connection exhaustion
80: - **Resolution**: Rolled back v2.3.4, increased pool size
81: - **Postmortem**: [POSTMORTEM-89](https://docs/postmortem-89)

88: ### Deployments

90: | Service      | Version | Time        | Notes                      |

95:

108: ## ⚠️ Known Issues & Workarounds
109: 
110: ### 1. Slow Dashboard Loading
111: 
112: **Issue**: Grafana dashboards slow on Monday mornings
113: **Workaround**: Wait 5 min after 08:00 UTC for cache warm-up
114: **Ticket**: OPS-456 (P3)

117: 
118: **Issue**: `test_payment_flow` fails intermittently in CI
119: **Workaround**: Re-run failed job (usually passes on retry)
120: **Ticket**: ENG-1200 (P2)

125:

135: 
136: | Issue Type      | First Escalation     | Second Escalation |
137: | --------------- | -------------------- | ----------------- |

145: ## 🔧 Quick Reference
146: 
147: ### Common Commands
148: 
149: ```bash
150: # Check service health
151: kubectl get pods -A | grep -v Running
152: 
153: # Recent deployments
154: kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -20
155: 
156: # Database connections
157: psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;"
158:

160: redis-cli FLUSHDB
161: ```
162: ````

165:

173: ## Handoff Checklist
174: 
175: ### Outgoing Engineer
176: 
177: - [x] Document active incidents
178: - [x] Document ongoing investigations
179: - [x] List recent changes
180: - [x] Note known issues
181: - [x] Add upcoming events
182: - [x] Sync with incoming engineer
183:

185:

187: - [ ] Join sync call

189: - [ ] Verify Slack notifications working

195: ### Template 2: Quick Handoff (Async)
196: 
197: ```markdown
198: # Quick Handoff: @alice → @bob
199: 
200: ## TL;DR
201: - No active incidents
202: - 1 investigation ongoing (API timeouts, see ENG-1234)
203: - Major release tomorrow (01/24) - be ready for issues
204: 
205: ## Watch List
206: 1. API latency around 02:00-03:00 UTC (backup window)
207: 2. Auth service memory (restart if > 80%)
208: 
209: ## Recent
210: - Deployed api-gateway v3.2.1 yesterday (stable)
211: - Increased rate limits to 1500 RPS
212: 
213: ## Coming Up
214: - 01/23 02:00 - DB maintenance (5 min read-only)
215: - 01/24 14:00 - v5.0 release
216: 
217: ## Questions?
218: I'll be available on Slack until 17:00 today.
219: ````

221: ### Template 3: Incident Handoff (Mid-Incident)
222: 
223: ```markdown
224: # INCIDENT HANDOFF: Payment Service Degradation
225: 
226: **Incident Start**: 2024-01-22 08:15 UTC
227: **Current Status**: Mitigating
228: **Severity**: SEV2
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## Current State
233: 
234: - Error rate: 15% (down from 40%)
235: - Mitigation in progress: scaling up pods
236: - ETA to resolution: ~30 min
237: 
238: ## What We Know
239: 
240: 1. Root cause: Memory pressure on payment-service pods
241: 2. Triggered by: Unusual traffic spike (3x normal)
242: 3. Contributing: Inefficient query in checkout flow
243: 
244: ## What We've Done
245: 
246: - Scaled payment-service from 5 → 15 pods
247: - Enabled rate limiting on checkout endpoint
248: - Disabled non-critical features
249: 
250: ## What Needs to Happen
251: 
252: 1. Monitor error rate - should reach <1% in ~15 min
253: 2. If not improving, escalate to @payments-manager
254: 3. Once stable, begin root cause investigation
255: 
256: ## Key People
257: 
258: - Incident Commander: @alice (handing off)
259: - Comms Lead: @charlie
260: - Technical Lead: @bob (incoming)
261: 
262: ## Communication
263: 
264: - Status page: Updated at 08:45
265: - Customer support: Notified
266: - Exec team: Aware"}}
